chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Ziyad, who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so a man said to him, 'May my father and mother be sacrificed for you! I enter my toilet, and I have neighbors who have slave girls who sing and strike with the oud. Sometimes I prolong my sitting to listen to them.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Do not do it.'

The man said, 'By Allah, I do not go to them; it is merely a sound that I hear with my ears.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'For the sake of Allah, have you not heard Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, saying: Indeed, the hearing and the sight and the heart, all of these will be questioned about?'
He said, 'Yes, by Allah! It is as if I had not heard this verse from the Book of Allah from a non-Arab nor an Arab. I will not return to it, if Allah wills, and I seek forgiveness from Allah.'

He (peace be upon him) said to him, 'Rise and perform ritual bath, and ask whatever comes to your mind, for you were standing upon a great matter. How evil would your state have been had you died upon that. Praise Allah and ask Him for repentance from everything He dislikes, for He does not dislike except every ugliness, and leave the ugliness for its people, for everything has its people.'

key_terms.الْفُؤاد: The heart or inner faculty of perception
key_terms.قَبِيح: Ugliness or that which is displeasing

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on listening to music or singing from neighbors in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Shia scholarly distinction between casual auditory perception and the spiritual accountability of the 'heart' (fu'ad), using the verse from Surah Al-Isra to elevate listening to music from a minor sensory act to a major sin requiring purification. The Imam’s instruction for ghusl underscores the ritual purity associated with repentance from significant spiritual negligence, while the phrase 'leave the ugly to its people' provides a practical framework for social coexistence without necessarily severing ties with non-Muslim or non-practicing neighbors.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Haroun Bin Muslim, from Mas’ada Bin Ziyad who said,

‘I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so a man said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May my father and my mother be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! I entered a toilet of mine and for me is a neighbour with whom are slave girls who are singing and striking with the sticks. So Sometimes I prolong my sitting in order to listen to them’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not do it’.

So the man said, ‘By Allahazwj! I do not go to them, but rather it is a sound which I hear with my ears’. So heasws said; ‘For the Sake of Allahazwj! You, have you not heard Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Saying [17:36] surely the hearing and the sight and the heart, all of these, shall be questioned about?’

So he said, ‘Yes, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! But, it is as if I never heard this verse from the Book of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, from neither non-Arabs, nor Arabs. I would not be repeating it, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Willing and I seek Forgiveness of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘Arise and wash, and ask whatever comes to you, for you are standing upon a great matter. How evil would your situation had been had you died upon that. Praise Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and ask Him<sup>asws</sup> for the repentance from everything which He<sup>azwj</sup> Dislikes, for He<sup>azwj</sup> does not Dislike except for every ugliness, and as for the ugliness, so leave it for its deserving ones, for everything there are deserving ones’.
en.sarwar: 10. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Harun ibn Muslim from Mas’adah ibn Ziyad who has said the following:

“Once I was with abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, when a man said, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul and the souls of my parents in service for your cause, I enter my WC (water-closet) and I have neighbors who have singing slave-girls who play musical instruments and perhaps I sit longer, listening to them.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘You must not do so.’

The man said, ‘By Allah, I do not go to them; it is only my listening to them with my ears.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘For the sake of Allah, have you not heard Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, saying, “...the ears, eyes, and hearts will all be held responsible for their deeds.” [17:36]’
He replied, ‘Yes, by Allah, as if I have not heard this verse of the book of Allah from non-Arab or Arab people. However, I will not return to it if Allah so wills and I ask forgiveness from Allah.

He (the Imam) said, ‘You must go and take a shower, then ask what you want, because you were involved in a great thing and how terrible your condition could have been had you remained in such condition! Praise Allah and ask Him to forgive you because of what He dislikes and He dislikes only bad and indecent matters; and you must leave evil and indecent things to indecent people; everything has its associates.’”
